threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still avoid the road when the buses are on strike. Everyone else just walks in the street like it’s a normal Tuesday.
Last Thursday, I saw a guy trying to sell a live goldfish on the 196. Said it would bring good luck. The fish didn't look too happy about it.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: It hit me when I saw the same balcony cat sunbathing every day, as the neighbor changed their plants with the seasons. That's home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a late-night kebab joint that serves up fresh salads topped with crispy falafel and a side of techno beats.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their nonchalant reaction to the BART delays. While newcomers panic, we just pull out our phones and check the next bus. It’s a way of life.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus this morning with a stray dog on board, just sitting there like it owned the place. Typical San Francisco vibe.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always flock to Park Güell, but they miss the quiet charm of Plaça del Sol. It's where we really unwind, not at those overcrowded spots.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at the lack of pedestrian crossings on Gran Via. They wait for traffic lights like it’s New York.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Overground', not the 'Ginger Line' like the locals do when discussing the best pubs nearby.
Caught a guy singing old school garage on the 59 last night, sounded just like a live DJ set. Half the bus was clapping along, only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a street vendor selling homemade samosas next to the punk band rehearsing in the park. That's when it hit me—this place is pure chaos and charm.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a currywurst at 3 AM right after a techno rave, with the street still pulsing and the kebab shops packed.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they know to avoid BART during rush hour after a brake failure. Tourists are still standing in line for a transfer.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling in front of a Muni bus that was late by 25 minutes. Didn’t miss a beat when the bus finally arrived—kept juggling as passengers groaned.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's squares are for lounging, but locals know they’re just a stage for the next round of protests or spontaneous concerts.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They walk into the local bakery and try to order 'pan' without knowing it's called 'barra' here. A true rookie move.
